rules.explanation: The system-wide cryptographic policy can be overridden or disabled for OpenSSH.
rules.impact: Overriding or opting out of the system-wide crypto policy may allow use of less secure ciphers, MACs, KexAlgorithms, and GSSAPIKexAlgorithm.

rules.title: NOPASSWD is not used in sudoers is configured
rules.explanation: Sudo must require the user password to prevent automatic privilege escalation.
rules.impact: NOPASSWD allows executing commands without authentication.

rules.title: Timestamp_timeout is set in /etc/sudoers to a value of no more than 15 minutes is configured
rules.explanation: Sudo must re-prompt for a password after a defined interval (typically 15 minutes).
rules.impact: A long session timeout increases the risk of an open session being abused.

rules.title: Sudo authentication uses the SHA-512 algorithm in the PAM configuration is configured
rules.explanation: Sudo authentication must use modern algorithms (for example SHA-512 in PAM).
rules.impact: Legacy MD5 methods are weakly protected.

rules.title: Access to the su command is restricted
rules.explanation: The su command allows a user to run a command or shell as another user. The program has been superseded by sudo, which provides more granular control over privileged access. Typically, the su command can be executed by any user. By uncommenting the pam_wheel.so statement in /etc/pam.d/su, the su command will allow only users in specified groups to execute su. This group should be empty to reinforce the use of sudo for privileged access.
rules.impact: Restricting use of su and using sudo instead gives system administrators better control over user privilege elevation for privileged commands. The sudo utility also provides a better logging and auditing mechanism because it can log every command executed via sudo, whereas su can record only that the user executed the su program.

rules.title: PASS_MAX_DAYS does not exceed 365 in /etc/login.defs is configured
rules.explanation: Regular password changes reduce the risk of compromise.
rules.impact: Unlimited password lifetime increases the risk of compromise.

rules.title: No unused files or directories exist
rules.explanation: Sometimes when administrators remove users from the password file, they forget to remove all files belonging to those users from the system.
rules.impact: A new user who is assigned a user or group identifier of deleted users may eventually "own" those files and thus have greater access to the system than intended.

rules.title: /etc/group contains no lines starting with the '+' character is configured
rules.explanation: "+" in /etc/group indicates a legacy NIS binding.
rules.impact: May result in unintended group membership.

rules.title: The nosuid option is set on the /dev/shm partition is configured
rules.explanation: The nosuid mount option indicates that the file system cannot contain setuid files.
rules.impact: Setting this option on the file system prevents users from introducing privileged programs onto the system and allowing non-root users to execute them.

rules.title: Package manager repositories are configured
rules.explanation: Systems must be configured with appropriate package manager repositories so that the system can receive the latest patches and updates.
rules.impact: If system package repositories are configured incorrectly, important patches may not be identified, or a rogue repository may contain compromised software.
rules.scope: Parameter for active and current repositories

rules.title: User shell timeout
rules.explanation: TMOUT by default defines the shell idle timeout for users. The TMOUT value is measured in seconds.
rules.impact: Setting a timeout value reduces the window of opportunity for unauthorized access to another user's shell session that has been left unattended. It also terminates an idle session and frees resources associated with that session.

rules.title: The disable-user-list option in GDM is enabled
rules.explanation: This option hides the user list on the logon screen.
rules.impact: Hiding the user list makes credential guessing more difficult.

rules.title: GDM screen lock on idle is configured
rules.explanation: The screen must lock after a period of inactivity.
rules.impact: This prevents unauthorized access if the user steps away.

rules.title: Prohibit canceling GDM screen lock
rules.explanation: Users must not be able to override the screen lock.
rules.impact: This makes bypassing protections more difficult.

rules.title: Automatic mounting of removable media in GDM is disabled
rules.explanation: USB device automounting can be dangerous.
rules.impact: This reduces the risk of executing malicious code from removable media.

rules.title: Prohibit overriding the disablement of automount in GDM
rules.explanation: Users must not be able to enable automounting.
rules.impact: Maintaining a stable security configuration.

rules.title: The autorun-never option in GDM is enabled
rules.explanation: This option prevents autorun of removable media contents.
rules.impact: Prevents execution of malicious code when devices are connected.

rules.title: Prohibit overriding autorun-never in GDM
rules.explanation: Users must not be able to disable this option.
rules.impact: Provides persistent protection against autorun.

rules.title: Daytime TCP/UDP services are disabled is configured
rules.explanation: The daytime service (ports 13/TCP and 13/UDP) returns the current system time in text form. This protocol is obsolete, does not require authentication, and must not be available on servers.
rules.impact: Legacy network services increase the attack surface.

rules.title: The SNMP server is not enabled is configured
rules.explanation: The Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) server is used to listen for SNMP, execute commands, or collect information and then send the results back to the requesting system.
rules.impact: An SNMP server can communicate using SNMP v1, which transmits data in the clear and does not require authentication to execute commands. If at all possible, it is recommended that the SNMP service not be used. If SNMP is required, the server should be configured to prohibit the use of SNMP v1.

rules.title: The telnet client is not installed is configured
rules.explanation: The telnet package contains the telnet client, which allows users to establish connections to other systems using the telnet protocol.
rules.impact: The telnet protocol is insecure and unencrypted. Use of unencrypted MEDIUM transmission may allow an unauthorized user to steal credentials.

rules.title: Send_redirects = 0 in /etc/sysctl.conf is configured
rules.explanation: The net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects parameter controls whether ICMP Redirects may be sent.
rules.impact: Enabled redirect packets allow an attacker to redirect traffic.

rules.title: Bluetooth services are disabled is configured
rules.explanation: Bluetooth can be an attack vector, especially on servers.
rules.impact: Disabling Bluetooth reduces the likelihood of attack.

rules.title: Iptables-persistent is not installed together with ufw is configured
rules.explanation: Ufw (Uncomplicated Firewall) and iptables-persistent are two different tools for managing the firewall. Using them together can lead to conflicts.
rules.impact: Using a single tool to manage the firewall simplifies configuration and reduces the risk of misconfiguration.

rules.title: Unsuccessful file access attempts are collected is configured
rules.explanation: Monitor unsuccessful file access attempts. The following parameters are associated with system calls that manage files: • create — create • open — open, openat • truncation — truncate, ftruncate. An audit log record will be written only if all of the following criteria are met for the user when attempting to access a file: • unprivileged user (auid>=UID_MIN) • not a Daemon event (auid=4294967295/unset/-1) • if the system call returned EACCES (access denied) or EPERM (some other persistent error associated with the specific system call).
rules.impact: Failed attempts to open, create, or truncate files may indicate that a user or process is attempting to gain unauthorized access to the system.

rules.title: Rsyslog is not configured to receive logs from a remote client is configured
rules.explanation: RSyslog supports receiving messages from remote hosts, thus acting as a log server. Clients must not receive data from other hosts.
rules.impact: If the client is also configured to receive data, turning it into a server, the client system operates outside its operational boundaries.

rules.title: The minimum number of days between password changes is 7 or more
rules.explanation: The PASS_MIN_DAYS parameter in /etc/login.defs allows an administrator to prevent users from changing their password until a minimum number of days have elapsed since the user last changed their password.
rules.impact: By limiting password-change frequency, an administrator can prevent users from repeatedly changing their password in an attempt to bypass password-reuse controls.

rules.title: PermitRootLogin is set to no or prohibit-password in /etc/ssh/sshd_config is configured
rules.explanation: Direct root login over SSH must be prohibited to prevent attacks against the superuser.
rules.impact: Permitting root login increases the risk of compromise.

rules.title: No /etc/shadow entries have an empty password field is configured
rules.explanation: /etc/shadow must not contain empty password fields.
rules.impact: An empty password field allows logon without authentication.

rules.title: /etc/passwd contains no lines starting with the '+' character is configured
rules.explanation: "+" entries in /etc/passwd indicate legacy NIS integration and must be removed.
rules.impact: Presence of "+" may enable unknown external accounts.

rules.title: No duplicate UIDs exist in /etc/passwd is configured
rules.explanation: UID must be unique for each user.
rules.impact: Duplicate UIDs allow users to act on behalf of others.

rules.title: No duplicate group names exist in /etc/group is configured
rules.explanation: Group names must be unique to avoid confusion in access rights and group policy control.
rules.impact: Duplicate group names make security management more difficult.

rules.title: No duplicate UIDs exist is configured
rules.explanation: Although the useradd program will not allow you to create a duplicate user identifier (UID), an administrator can manually edit /etc/passwd and change the UID field.
rules.impact: Users must be assigned unique UIDs for accountability and to ensure proper access protection.

rules.title: Audit log files contain information about the system and system activity is configured
rules.explanation: Audit log files contain information about the system and system activity.
rules.impact: Access to audit records may disclose system and configuration data to attackers, which may compromise their confidentiality.

rules.title: The audit log directory contains audit log files is configured
rules.explanation: The audit log directory contains audit log files.
rules.impact: Audit information includes all information, including audit records, audit settings, and audit reports. This information is required for successful auditing of system activity. This information must be protected from unauthorized modification or deletion. If this information is compromised, forensic analysis and identification of the true source of potentially malicious system activity will be impossible.

rules.title: Audit configuration files control auditing and which events are audited is configured
rules.explanation: Audit configuration files control auditing and which events are audited.
rules.impact: Access to audit configuration files may allow unauthorized personnel to prevent auditing of critical events.

rules.title: Audit configuration files control auditing and which events are audited is configured
rules.explanation: Audit configuration files control auditing and which events are audited.
rules.impact: Access to audit configuration files may allow unauthorized personnel to prevent auditing of critical events.

rules.title: Audit configuration files control auditing and which events are audited is configured
rules.explanation: Audit configuration files control auditing and which events are audited.
rules.impact: Access to audit configuration files may allow unauthorized personnel to prevent auditing of critical events.

rules.title: Audit tools have permissions of 755 or more restrictive is configured
rules.explanation: Audit tools include, but are not limited to, open-source and vendor-provided audit tools required to successfully view and manage audit information system activities and records. Audit tools include custom queries and report generators.
rules.impact: Protecting audit information includes identifying and protecting tools used to view and manage log data. Protection of audit tools is necessary to prevent unauthorized operations on audit information.
rules.scope: Parameters and permissions of the utilities /sbin/auditctl /sbin/aureport /sbin/ausearch /sbin/autrace /sbin/auditd /sbin/augenrules

rules.title: Audit tools are owned by the root user is configured
rules.explanation: Audit tools include, but are not limited to, open-source and vendor-provided audit tools required to successfully view and manage audit information system activities and records. Audit tools include custom queries and report generators.
rules.impact: Protecting audit information includes identifying and protecting tools used to view and manage log data. Protection of audit tools is necessary to prevent unauthorized operations on audit information.
rules.scope: Permissions and root ownership for the utilities /sbin/auditctl /sbin/aureport /sbin/ausearch /sbin/autrace /sbin/auditd /sbin/augenrules

rules.title: Audit tools are owned by the root group is configured
rules.explanation: Audit tools include, but are not limited to, open-source and vendor-provided audit tools required to successfully view and manage audit information system activities and records. Audit tools include custom queries and report generators.
rules.impact: Protecting audit information includes identifying and protecting tools used to view and manage log data. Protection of audit tools is necessary to prevent unauthorized operations on audit information.
rules.scope: Permissions and the root group for the utilities /sbin/auditctl /sbin/aureport /sbin/ausearch /sbin/autrace /sbin/auditd /sbin/augenrules

rules.title: Successful file system mount operations are recorded is configured
rules.explanation: Auditing successful file system mounts allows tracking of external media attachment and mounting of network resources, which is an important security event.
rules.impact: Unauthorized mounting of removable media or a network resource without auditing allows an attacker to covertly attach a device to steal data or introduce malicious code.
